linkedin.title: Our friends at @[Resonate HQ](urn:li:organization:99146314) have a really cool use case with us.
linkedin.description:
Our friends at @[Resonate HQ](urn:li:organization:99146314) have a really cool use case with us.

Imagine a worker that pulls tasks from one queue and pushes results to another:

Two common issues:
- Head-of-line blocking: A long task blocks shorter ones unless the worker runs tasks concurrently.
- Crash recovery: If the worker crashes mid-task, it may redo work, causing duplication or errors.

A good worker should:
- Run tasks in parallel
- Resume safely after failure

Check out this Redpanda + Resonate example. Resonate handles both problems, extending Redpanda’s durability without blocking progress. https://lnkd.in/gBrsP6TH

video_groups.canonical_title: What #agent Infrastructure Actually Looks Like #programming #coding #code #aiagents
video_groups.description:
Everyone's talking about AI agents. Almost nobody is showing what the infrastructure underneath them looks like.

Check out the full length version of this video on YouTube: https://youtu.be/0ybk-ri7T-A

For agents to actually work in an enterprise, they need:
 ⁃ Live access to your real data (not a static dump)
 ⁃ A standard protocol for interacting with tools
 ⁃ A full record of every decision they make

That's agent infrastructure. And it's the part that determines whether your agent deployment makes it past the POC.

#AIAgents #AgentInfrastructure #MCP #DataStreaming

video_groups.canonical_title: Teams often store logs and event data in Amazon {hashtag|\#|S3}. That data is valuable, but locked in a format that’s
video_groups.description:
Teams often store logs and event data in Amazon {hashtag|\#|S3}. That data is valuable, but locked in a format that’s difficult to operationalize for real-time use. 💢 

If you want to drive live dashboards, trigger alerts, or feed {hashtag|\#|AI} pipelines, you need a way to turn that cold, static {hashtag|\#|data} into a live stream. 🛶 

In just a minute, learn how to use Redpanda Connect to stream and transform CSV data from S3 into a Redpanda Serverless topic. 

We’ll walk through:
☑️ Ingesting CSV files from an S3 bucket
☑️ Normalizing and cleaning up the data \(including stripping sensitive fields\)
☑️ Publishing the results to Redpanda for downstream processing

By the end, you’ll have a working data pipeline that runs continuously and can be deployed in minutes!
